items.title: Case Summary: Alkegen Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Alkegen, the Clearlake-backed specialty materials maker formed in Unifrax's debt-funded 2021 acquisition of Lydall, filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 to shed roughly $3.1B of its $3.5B of funded debt, with first lien creditors taking substantially all of the reorganized equity.

items.title: Case Summary: Republic National Distributing Company Chapter 11
items.excerpt: RNDC, until recently the second-largest U.S. beverage alcohol distributor, filed Chapter 11 after post-pandemic demand declines and supplier losses eroded liquidity. Having sold 11 markets to Reyes, it now seeks to sell the rest and confirm a plan built on a settlement with its founding families.

items.title: Case Summary: Magellan Aerospace Middletown Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Magellan Aerospace, Middletown filed for Chapter 11 after legacy aircraft programs wound down with no replacements and decades-old environmental liabilities at former California sites triggered mounting cleanup orders and an adverse jury verdict, exploring a standalone restructuring or sale.

items.title: Case Summary: Poolin Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Poolin, once the world's largest Bitcoin mining pool, and affiliates filed for Chapter 11 after a 2022 liquidity crisis froze customer withdrawals and left ~$163.7M in wallet-holder IOUs; its West Texas mining sites, which never reached scale, are now being marketed for sale under a §363 process.

items.title: Case Summary: CashCall Chapter 11
items.excerpt: CashCall, a subprime consumer lender, filed Chapter 11 after two consumer-finance judgments totaling roughly $402.6M, seeking $4M of financing from an owner-controlled affiliate while evaluating a potential estate claim concerning a 2021 distribution to that same owner.

items.title: Case Summary: Alea Holdings Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Alea Holdings US Company and affiliates, non-operating holdcos in Catalina Holdings' runoff platform, filed Chapter 11 after non-Debtor SPARTA was left holding legacy AEIC liabilities and a TruPS tender fell short, pursuing an RSA-backed plan and 363 sales of equity in two non-Debtor insurers.

items.title: Case Summary: Pacifica Hospital of the Valley Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Pacifica Hospital of the Valley, a Los Angeles safety-net hospital, filed for Chapter 11 to halt a creditor's contested loan-to-own bid for control and a pending receivership, after a liquidity crisis, pandemic costs, seismic-retrofit fines, and delayed government payments eroded operations.

items.title: Case Summary: DISH DBS & DISH Wireless Chapter 11
items.excerpt: DISH DBS and DISH Wireless, EchoStar subsidiaries, filed dual-track Chapter 11 cases to reorganize the declining DISH/Sling pay-TV business and wind down DISH Wireless via a §363 sale, after the FCC pressed EchoStar to sell the spectrum licenses needed for the 5G network or face license forfeiture.

items.title: Case Summary: TPx Communications Chapter 11
items.excerpt: TPx Communications filed for Chapter 11 unable to service roughly $1.1B in debt, pursuing an RSA-backed dual-track restructuring — a Section 363 sale or a lender- and sponsor-led reorganization that would leave the managed IT services provider with about $129M of funded debt and preferred equity.

items.title: Case Summary: Damis Holdings Chapter 11
items.excerpt: DAMIS Holdings, the real-estate arm of the Shabsels brothers' enterprise, filed a free-fall Chapter 11 with 89 affiliates amid its BVI parent's bond default, acute liquidity distress, and MCA lenders sweeping accounts.

items.title: Case Summary: Sangamo Therapeutics Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Sangamo Therapeutics filed for Chapter 11 after losing its major collaboration revenues and exhausting its liquidity, pursuing a court-supervised sale with stalking-horse bids from Lilly for its core platforms and Astellas for its Fabry program.

items.title: Case Summary: Hallmark Financial Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Hallmark Financial filed Chapter 11 to sell its business or swap controlling creditor Hildene's debt for equity, after reserve failures, a lost reinsurance arbitration, and a ratings collapse gutted its equity—tripping a senior-note covenant Hildene wouldn't waive, foreclosing an out-of-court fix.

items.title: Case Summary: Searles Valley Minerals Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Searles Valley Minerals filed Chapter 11 to pursue a §363 going-concern sale of its business — anchored by its Trona, CA mining complex — after 2019 Ridgecrest earthquake damage, soda ash oversupply and price collapse, and mounting losses left it no viable out-of-court path.

items.title: Case Summary: SIMAD Holdings Chapter 11
items.excerpt: SIMAD Holdings filed Chapter 11 to pursue an expedited financing or sale of its 30-camp portfolio, after missing a May 31 interest payment on $214M in Tel Aviv bonds following a ~$34M owner transfer under investigation and facing cash seizure by merchant cash advance lenders.

items.title: Case Summary: Sleep Number Chapter 11
items.excerpt: Sleep Number filed Chapter 11 to sell its assets to Fairfax-owned Sleep Country Canada for $415M through a lender-backed Section 363 process, after a multi-year mattress recession and a pandemic-era balance sheet left the smart-bed maker with roughly $672.5M of funded debt it could no longer carry.
